practices.title: Salesforce Data 360 Credit Optimization Guide
practices.summary: 19 concrete techniques for cutting Data Cloud credit consumption across ingestion, transformation, identity resolution, segmentation, and activation - from defaulting to batch over streaming to Digital Wallet consumption alerts.

points.text: Filter data upstream before ingestion - remove records with null values in critical fields (email, phone) and limit to active customers from the last 12-24 months rather than ingesting complete historical records.

Default to batch processing over streaming - streaming calculated insights cost up to 53x more than batch (800 vs. 15 credits per million rows). Reserve streaming exclusively for decisions requiring sub-15-minute latency like fraud detection or in-session personalization.
Ingest only necessary fields - avoid bringing in all available columns; map activation use cases to specific required fields.
Optimize calculated insight refresh schedules - adjust frequency based on time sensitivity: hourly for real-time metrics, daily for routine decisions, weekly for static reports.
points.impact: Moving hourly to weekly saves ~99.4% of insight costs

points.text: Deactivate unused segments and data streams - audit regularly and remove outdated segments, insights, and data flows that no longer deliver business value but continue consuming credits on scheduled refreshes.
Refine identity resolution match rules for precision - use exact matching criteria (exact email, exact phone) before fuzzy matching to prevent unifying unrelated records.

Monitor profile count growth continuously - track how new ingestions impact existing unified profile counts to detect overly broad matching rules or data quality issues creating unnecessary duplicates.
Design data models for consumption patterns, not storage - group related fields that will be accessed together into single data model objects to minimize join complexity.
Nest common segment filters - create base segments (e.g. high-value active customers) and build sub-segments that filter from it, avoiding reprocessing the full population for each variation.
Reduce segment refresh frequency - switching a 50-million-row segment from daily to weekly refresh has acceptable freshness for most campaigns.
Consolidate activation destinations - each destination incurs separate activation costs; consolidate multiple destinations where possible to avoid running redundant activation cycles.
Limit enrichment attributes in activations - include only attributes the destination system actually uses for personalization; additional attributes increase data traversal costs.
Monitor identity resolution costs via Digital Wallet - track IR credit consumption specifically to understand how unification decisions impact overall spending.
Use Digital Wallet consumption alerts - configure Flow-based threshold notifications at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 90% of allocated credits to prevent unexpected overspend.
Build custom consumption reports - analyze TenantEnrichedUsageEvent data to identify top-consuming data streams, transforms, and segments, and correlate credit spend with business value delivered.
Disable unnecessary data streams in sandbox environments - sandbox usage now consumes production credits; disable replicated data streams in sandboxes to prevent unintended credit drain.
Evaluate federation vs. ingestion based on access frequency - if accessing external data more than ~29 times, ingesting once becomes cheaper than federating each time.
Define high-impact use cases before ingesting data - lock in data classification decisions upfront; changing classifications later requires re-ingestion and re-transformation at full credit cost.

Use the Salesforce pricing calculator - model expected usage across all three pricing models (credit-based, profile-based SKUs, flex credits) before building to estimate total cost of ownership accurately.
